c.tagline: A gateway to dramatic limestone karsts and turquoise Andaman Sea coves, from Railay's cliffs to nearby islands

card: Accepted at larger hotels and restaurants; cash preferred at markets and beach vendors

taxi.fare: Negotiated flat rate; Grab available in town
taxi.fareNote: Longtail boats, not taxis, are the way to reach Railay Beach (no road access)

emergency.note: Tourist police (1155) can assist with English-language support

religion: Islam (significant minority, especially in southern Thailand)

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Krabi Town's riverside and night market are walkable; Railay, Ao Nang, and the islands require a longtail boat, songthaew, or organized tour

safety.safety: Generally safe and tourism-oriented; standard beach and boat-safety precautions apply
safety.crime: Petty theft on crowded beaches and overcharging by unlicensed boat operators are the main concerns

hood_landmark.Ao Nang: Ao Nang's beachfront promenade of hotels and dive shops
hood_landmark.Railay Beach: Railay's sheer limestone cliffs and rock climbing routes
hood_landmark.Hong / Four Islands (boat-trip base): The Four Islands' turquoise coves and limestone karsts

avoid.reason: Motorbike rental-damage scams; scooter-accident risk; drink-spiking in nightlife

hood_desc: The practical provincial capital with the night market, riverside walkway, and long-distance transport hub, less touristy than the beach areas.
The area's main beach resort strip, packed with hotels, dive shops, and restaurants, and the jumping-off point for island boat tours.
A stunning cliff-backed peninsula reachable only by boat, world-famous for rock climbing and its beach bars.
A hilltop temple complex a short drive from town, with a steep climb rewarded by panoramic karst views.
A cluster of postcard-perfect islands reached by longtail or speedboat from Ao Nang, essential for a day of swimming and snorkeling.
lodging: Boutique hotels near the night market
Centara Grand Beach Resort & Villas Krabi

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap is not potable.

transit.sys: Songthaews (shared pickup trucks) around Krabi Town and to Ao Nang; longtail boats to Railay and the islands
transit.map: Not centrally published; songthaews and boats run frequent informal routes
transit.note: Railay Beach has no road access; longtail boats from Ao Nang or Krabi Town are the only way in

transport.air: Krabi International Airport (KBV), about 20 min from Krabi Town
transport.train: No passenger rail service to Krabi
transport.bus: Long-distance buses connect to Bangkok (about 12 hr), Phuket, and Surat Thani
transport.ferry: Ferries connect Krabi to Phi Phi Islands, Koh Lanta, and Phuket
transport.car: Rental cars and scooters available; roads connect Krabi Town and Ao Nang directly

net.m: Good 4G coverage in town and Ao Nang, patchier on remote islands
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: An AIS or DTAC tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory but appreciated for guides and boat operators
